title: VR Project Brings Hope to Kids in Japan Hospitals
paragraphs: A long stay in hospital is never fun, but for a homesick child missing their family and school friends, it can feel especially lonely — and scary.
But like anyone spending a long time in hospital, kids need more than medical treatment — they need hope.
Now, more than 30 hospitals in Japan are promoting a project that hopes to provide just that using virtual reality (VR).
In mid-July, around 100 children from hospitals across Japan put on headsets and met up together in a VR recreation of Osaka's Tennoji Zoo.
The kids, aged between 4 and 16, could freely explore the zoo and communicate with each other using text messages and emoji.
While listening to explanations from zookeepers, the kids could see giraffes and zebras, a lion roaring on top of a rock, and a hippo swimming in a tank full of fish.

A childcare worker at Okayama University Hospital, where 15 children took part, told Kyodo News that even kids who normally didn't have the energy to leave their rooms managed to take part because they were looking forward to it so much.
The virtual zoo was created by Kintetsu Real Estate and metaverse developer Cluster. Project organizers hope to add more virtual spaces for children to explore in the future.
Joe Hasei, a professor at Okayama University who is leading the project, told Kyodo News that he hopes experiences like this could help children with serious illnesses feel less alone.
"I hope it helps them approach treatment with a positive outlook and think, 'When I leave hospital, I'm going to visit the real Tennoji Zoo,'" he added.
